sections.content:
English says 'I want you to come', but Spanish says 'I want that you come' (Quiero que vengas).

• Rule 1 (1 subject): When the subject doesn't change, use the INFINITIVE: 'Yo quiero comer' (I want to eat).
• Rule 2 (2 subjects): When you want someone ELSE to do something, use QUE + SUBJUNCTIVE: 'Yo quiero que TÚ comas' (I want you to eat).

sections.title: 1 Subject vs. 2 Subjects
rows: Necesito que me ayudes. (I need you to help me.)
Prefiero salir temprano. (I prefer to leave early.)
Prefiero que salgamos juntos. (I prefer that we leave together.)

items.spanish: Mi jefe me pide que termine el informe hoy.
items.english: My boss asks me to finish the report today.

items.spanish: ¿Quieres que te acompañe a la estación?
items.english: Do you want me to accompany you to the station?
